editorial:
Imagine coming home from a war zone only to find that the real battle is happening inside your own head. You follow Suzy, a British soldier who returns from Iraq with a heavy weight on her shoulders. She cannot stop thinking about a child who died while she was on duty, and that guilt starts to warp how she sees her own life. The vibe is very tense and heavy, making you feel the pressure she is under as she tries to be a good mom while fighting off scary thoughts. It is a sad look at how war changes a person and how hard it is to just switch back to being a normal citizen.

What really hits home is the acting, as you can see Suzy slowly losing her grip on reality. The pacing starts slow but builds up to a breaking point that feels real and scary. While some might find the slow build frustrating, it makes the ending feel earned. If you enjoy deep character studies, you should definitely check this out. You can rent it on Apple TV for a quick watch, or if you want the best picture quality, try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to catch all the small details in her expressions.
endingExplained: Everything falls apart when Suzy's fear for her daughter turns into a full crisis. Her need to protect the girl becomes so extreme that she actually puts her child in a dangerous spot. The movie ends with a heartbreaking realization that the biggest threat to the child was actually Suzy's own broken mind. It wraps up by showing that without the right help, the trauma from war can destroy the things we love most.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about mental health and family struggles.
